events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: Barnstable; Nantucket
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways (3.2 to 11.6 feet Mean Lower Low Water).

* WHERE...Barnstable MA and Nantucket MA Counties.

* WHEN...Friday afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Roads remain passable. Low lying areas and roads
near Nantucket Harbor, including Easy Street, may experience
pockets of shallow flooding less than one foot deep.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Splashover and very minor coastal flooding
are possible during the Friday afternoon high tide along north
facing beaches on Cape Cod Bay as well as Nantucket sound. No
significant impacts are expected and any splashover/very minor
coastal flooding will be quite short-lived, no more than an hour
on either side of high tide.

events.title: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.region: McMullen, TX
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
...The National Weather Service in Corpus Christi has issued a Flood
Warning for the following rivers in Texas...

Nueces River Near Tilden affecting McMullen County.

For the Nueces River...including Tilden...Minor flooding is forecast.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Sunday afternoon until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below Cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.
Hunting cabins, oil field pump jacks and tank batteries flood well
away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 7:30 AM CST Thursday the stage was 8.5 feet.
- Bankfull stage is 11.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage early
Sunday afternoon and continue rising to a crest of 15.0 feet
Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- Flood History...This crest compares to a previous crest of 15.2
feet on 09/19/1983.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

events.region: Northeast Siskiyou and Northwest Modoc Counties; Modoc County; Klamath Basin; Northern and Eastern Klamath County and Western Lake County; Central and Eastern Lake County
events.source_name: US National Weather Service Active Alerts
events.summary:
* WHAT...South winds 25 to 35 mph with gusts up to 55 mph expected.

* WHERE...In California, Modoc and Northeast Siskiyou and Northwest
Modoc Counties Counties. In Oregon, Central and Eastern Lake,
Klamath Basin, and Northern and Eastern Klamath and Western Lake
Counties. Winds will be strongest near Summer Lake on Highway 31.

* WHEN...From 10 PM this evening to 4 PM PST Friday.

* IMPACTS...Gusty winds will blow around unsecured objects. Tree
limbs could be blown down and a few power outages may result.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Highways running west to east will be exposed
to tough driving conditions given the strong southerly wind speeds.
